topic: The Central Limit Theorem (CLT): The Magic of Averages

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Distribution
lecture_lines: A distribution shows how data spreads out.
Uniform distributions mean all outcomes are equally likely.
Rolling a die creates a uniform distribution.
animations: Highlight "A distribution shows how data spreads out." in #FF00FF and visualize a scatter plot in #FFFFFF.
Highlight "Uniform distributions mean all outcomes are equally likely." in #FF00FF and animate a flat horizontal bar chart in #FFFF00.
Highlight "Rolling a die creates a uniform distribution." in #FF00FF and show [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/die.svg] spinning.

sections.title: The Hook: The Chaos of One vs. The Order of Many
lecture_lines: What happens when we average multiple samples?
One sample is random and chaotic.
animations: Highlight "What happens when we average multiple samples?" in #FF00FF and display [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/dice.svg].
Highlight "One sample is random and chaotic." in #FF00FF and show a scattered point animation in #FF5555.
Highlight "Many samples averaged become predictable." in #FF00FF and show [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/coins.svg] stacking into a stable shape.

sections.title: Core Concept: The Normal Approximation
lecture_lines: Sample means approach a normal distribution.
This happens regardless of population shape.
Increase sample size for better approximation.
animations: Highlight "The CLT explains this magic." in #FF00FF and show a transition arrow in #FFFFFF.
Highlight "Sample means approach a normal distribution." in #FF00FF and draw a normal curve in #00FF00.
Highlight "This happens regardless of population shape." in #FF00FF and animate different source shapes transforming.
Highlight "Increase sample size for better approximation." in #FF00FF and show narrowing distribution in #FFFF00.
Highlight "The bell curve always emerges." in #FF00FF and display [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bell.svg] clearly.

sections.title: Visualizing the Bell Curve
lecture_lines: Two key parameters emerge: mean and variance.
The mean of means equals population mean.
Variance shrinks as sample size grows.
animations: Highlight "Two key parameters emerge: mean and variance." in #FF00FF and show [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/curve.svg] with mean and variance labels.
Highlight "The mean of means equals population mean." in #FF00FF and align two lines for comparison in #FFFFFF.
Highlight "Variance shrinks as sample size grows." in #FF00FF and animate distribution tightening with [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bell.svg].

sections.title: Application: Real-World Predictability
lecture_lines: CLT allows population inference from samples.
We predict outcomes without knowing original shapes.
It bridges sample data to real-world certainty.
animations: Highlight "CLT allows population inference from samples." in #FF00FF and show [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/population.svg].
Highlight "We predict outcomes without knowing original shapes." in #FF00FF and display an inference cloud in #FFFFFF.
Highlight "It bridges sample data to real-world certainty." in #FF00FF and show [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bridge.svg] connecting samples to certainty.
